THIS PETITION IS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE HEMANT  CHANDANGOUDAR  ORAL ORDER 1.

The petitioners, who are facing charges for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 307, 323,
504, and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short, 'IPC') and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, have approached this Court seeking quashing of the proceedings initiated against them.

sentences.text: The prosecution's case is that accused No.1 is the husband, accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents-in-law, and accused No.4 is the brother-in-law of the defacto complainant.
It is alleged that they subjected the complainant to both physical and mental cruelty and that accused No.3 made an attempt to murder her.
Further, all the accused allegedly demanded money from the complainant's parental house.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the petition papers.
4.
This Court, by an interim order dated 07.02.2022, stayed the proceedings against accused Nos.3 and 4 while allowing the trial Court to proceed against accused Nos.1 and 2.
During the pendency of this petition, the trial Court acquitted accused Nos.1 and 2 by judgment dated 27.11.2024.
5. Upon examining the allegations, it is observed that the charges against accused Nos.3 and 4 are general and omnibus in nature, with no specific overt act attributed to them.
Additionally, it is undisputed that accused Nos.3 and 4 reside separately from the complainant.
Furthermore, accused Nos.1 and 2, against whom specific allegations were made, have already been acquitted by the trial Court.
In light of these facts, the continuation of criminal proceedings against accused Nos.3 and 4 would amount to an abuse of the process of law.
